answer: Each identity must be anchored to one physical address: the network mails a tamper-evident letter with a one-time code, like a relic of registration, and one address holds one identity. Virtual mailboxes and forwarding services are blacklisted once detected, with re-verification every few epochs. No digital trick crosses the canyon of last-mile delivery — a spoofer cannot conjure N real doorbells, so N sockpuppets means renting or bribing N real addresses, each with its own paper thread of bills and tenancy records. The attacker pays per address, linearly; an honest user opens one envelope.
